agree.reason: The matched-gift arithmetic and the honest 26-of-61 framing make a concrete case, but someone still hurt about Eastside gets one short paragraph and a pivot to 'look who is waiting now,' which may feel like being told to move on.

honest.reason: It drops the brief's false promise of a place for every child and gets the sums right ($30,000 ÷ $1,150 ≈ 26), but it says 'many of you told us' when only 'a few' wrote, and the P.S. claim that 'any amount… counts double' leaves out the $15,000 cap.

works_the_facts.reason: Turning $85 into $170, $575 into one child's year and the full match into 26 children is useful, but it never sets the target against last December's 9 gifts and $1,240, which shows how far the match is from being met.

right_comparison.reason: It never says what happens if this group gives at last year's rate (about $2,500 including the match, roughly two children) or that the other children simply stay on the list, so the reader has no real alternative to weigh.

qualification.reason: The condition is checkable, with a date (December 31), a number (26 children if the full $30,000 is reached) and a stated shortfall against 61, but it doesn't say what happens to the match money or the children if the match falls short.

objections.reason: It names the Eastside closure and accepts the anger, but it gives no reason for the closure and doesn't say whether Eastside families are among those waiting, so the core grievance goes unanswered.

fit.reason: It's a year-end appeal of about 240 words with a subject line, a call to action, a P.S. and the executive director's signature, as the brief asked.
